description: Fix the visual fidelity defects the user reported by comparing every output/compare/*.jpg cell-by-cell against its reference: (a) cell/text background colours that are wrong or dropped (notably the peach/orange tint washes on DIVISION PERFORMANCE data cells that currently render white), (b) the deterministic competency-level background colour, and (c) unmerged cells whose long text overflows its box. Depends on FEAT-001 (needs a green baseline). All work MUST preserve the existing 100% text similarity + glyphs=identical guarantee.
steps: Diagnose the dropped-background bug in src/sars/extract.py `_pick_background`. It only accepts a fill whose area is >=55% of the cell bbox and picks the SMALLEST such fill. In the DIVISION PERFORMANCE band the tint (e.g. #fde9d9 peach, #fabf8f orange) is often drawn as a per-column strip that is narrower or shorter than the individual F/M/T cell, so it fails the 55% test and the cell renders white. Confirm with: `python tools/probe.py 'MWANZA CC 10 BEST SCHOOLS'` and by dumping harvest_fills vs kept cell.style.background for page 1 (a scratch script). Adjust the fill-to-cell matching so a tint that plausibly underlies the cell centre and shares the cell's colour is applied: e.g. lower/replace the strict area ratio with a rule that also accepts a fill covering the cell's horizontal OR vertical extent, or that accepts the dominant non-white fill overlapping the cell centre by a smaller threshold. Do NOT reintroduce table rule lines (#000000 / near-black) or the page wash / panel as cell backgrounds - keep those exclusions. Verify the peach tints now appear on the DIVISION PERFORMANCE data cells in the regenerated compare image.

Encode the deterministic competency-level background as an explicit mapping and use it as the authoritative colour for competency cells (falling back to extraction only when no competency band is detected). The observed canonical mapping across the reports is: 'Excellent'/'Grade A' -> #00b050; 'Very Good'/'Grade B' -> #92d050; 'Good'/'Grade C' -> #ffff00; 'Satisfactory'/'Grade D' -> #ffc000 (some reports draw it as #eeb500/#daf2d0 variants); 'Fail'/'Weak'/'Grade F' -> #ff0000. The band cutoffs follow the Tanzanian GPA competency scale the user described (approx 1.0-1.5 Excellent, 1.6-2.5 Very Good, 2.6-3.5 Good, 3.6-4.5 Satisfactory, 4.6-5.0 Fail). Add a small module (e.g. src/sars/competency.py) with a function mapping a competency label (and/or GPA value) to (label_text, background_hex), plus the band cutoffs [1.5,2.5,3.5,4.5]. IMPORTANT: verify the exact hex per report against the actual reference PDFs before hard-coding (dump the backgrounds of competency-labelled cells across all reports); if a report uses a different palette, key the mapping so the extracted colour still wins when it disagrees, so no report regresses. This mapping is reused by the templates in FEAT-004.

Fix the cell-merge / overflow defect in src/sars/html_out.py. The DOC_CSS rule `th,td{...white-space:nowrap;overflow:visible...}` makes long values (long SCHOOL NAME, COMPETENCY LEVEL text) overhang the ruled cell instead of wrapping. Make the structure ELASTIC: allow wrapping where a cell's content is longer than its column so text stays inside the box. Change the default to allow wrapping (e.g. white-space:normal; overflow-wrap:break-word; word-break where needed) for text/label cells, while keeping nowrap only where the PDF genuinely overhangs a narrow ruled cell (the rotated rank labels via .rot, and any column the extractor marks as intentionally overhanging). Because row height is currently taken verbatim from the PDF via line-height, ensure wrapping does not silently drop rows: prefer letting a wrapped cell grow its row (remove the fixed single-line line-height on cells that may wrap) OR widen the elastic handling so verification still passes. After the change, re-run `sars verify` for the affected documents and confirm text similarity stays 100% and glyphs=identical (no rows dropped).

Also audit and, where they are genuinely unmerged in the output but merged in the reference, fix cell merging in classify.py/extract.py (colspan/rowspan). Use the compare images to identify any header or label cell that should span but is split. Only change merging where the reference clearly shows a merged cell; do not over-merge.

Regenerate output and comparison images for a representative spread and inspect them cell-by-cell against the reference: at minimum 'MWANZA CC 10 BEST SCHOOLS' (peach tints), 'MWANZA CC SCHOOLS RANK SUBJECTWISE' and 'MWANZA CC SUBJECTS RANK' (competency colour bands incl. red Fail), 'S1051-MKOLANI SECONDARY SCHOOL' (cyan panel), and one long-name report to confirm wrapping. Commands: `sars all --only "<name>"` then `python tools/compare.py "<name>" <page>`.

Record in findings: the specific extract.py change made, the competency mapping module and cutoffs, the CSS wrapping change, and a before/after note on which compare images now match colours cell-for-cell.
acceptance_criteria: In the regenerated 'MWANZA CC 10 BEST SCHOOLS - page 1.jpg', the DIVISION PERFORMANCE data cells carry the same peach/orange tint washes as the reference (they are no longer white).

Competency-level cells render the correct deterministic background per band across the reports that colour them (green Excellent, light-green Very Good, yellow Good, orange Satisfactory, red Fail), matching the reference.
Long cell values (e.g. long SCHOOL NAME / COMPETENCY LEVEL text) wrap inside their cell box instead of overflowing, visible in the compare images.
`sars verify` (via `sars all`) still reports 19/19 pass, mean text similarity 100.00%, glyphs=identical for every document (no data dropped by wrapping).
A new module encodes the competency band->colour mapping and is importable for reuse by the templates.
verification: python tools/compare.py "MWANZA CC SCHOOLS RANK SUBJECTWISE" 1
findings:
Implemented on branch main; NOT committed (orchestrator commits). Final state: `sars all` = 19/19 pass, mean text similarity 100.00%, glyphs=identical for every document; `pytest -q` = 29 passed (25 prior + 4 new competency tests); ruff + black clean on src/ and tests/.

DIAGNOSIS (dropped tint backgrounds, step 1): Verified with a scratch dump of harvest_fills vs kept cell.style.background across MWANZA CC 10 BEST SCHOOLS, SCHOOLS RANK SUBJECTWISE, SUBJECTS RANK, schools rank Overall, Top 10 Schools. After FEAT-001 there were ZERO cells where a non-white fill overlapped the cell centre yet was rejected by the 55% area rule (checked explicitly). The DIVISION PERFORMANCE tint washes (#fde9d9 peach, #fabf8f orange, #d2fce6, #ccffff, etc.) are drawn per-cell or as 3-cell F/M/T strips; each strip's area is ~3x a single cell, so it comfortably passes the >=55% test and covers each cell centre. Confirmed cell-by-cell in the regenerated compare image that the peach/orange/blue washes now appear on the DIVISION PERFORMANCE cells matching the reference. No change to _pick_background's area rule was needed and none was made (changing it risked regressing the exact-100% text guarantee); the 55% + centre-overlap + white/near-black exclusions were left intact so table rules and the page wash/panel are still never used as cell backgrounds.

COMPETENCY MODULE (step 2): Added src/sars/competency.py. Verified the exact hex per label by dumping backgrounds of every competency-labelled cell across all 19 reports: Grade A (Excellent) -> #00b050 (58), Grade B (Very Good) -> #92d050 (145), Grade C (Good) -> #ffff00 (244), Grade D (Satisfactory) -> #ffc000 (330) with #eeb500/#e26b0a/#daf2d0 variants, Grade F (Fail) -> #ff0000 (230); single-word 'Excellent'/'Good'/'Satisfactory'/'Fail' and 'Weak'/'Failed' synonyms also present. IMPORTANT palette conflict found: some reports paint 'Very Good' YELLOW (#ffff00 x20) not light-green, so a pure deterministic mapping would regress them. Module therefore stores canonical BANDS + CUTOFFS=(1.5,2.5,3.5,4.5) + KNOWN_VARIANTS, and exposes band_for_gpa / band_for_label / resolve / background_for for reuse by FEAT-004 templates. In extract.build_table the deterministic colour is applied ONLY as a fallback when _pick_background returns None for a competency cell, so the EXTRACTED colour always wins and no report regresses. band_for_label matches single-token labels by exact equality and multi-word competency phrases ('Grade A', 'Very Good', ...) by whole-word containment; earlier substring matching wrongly tinted SCHOOL NAME cells like 'ALLIANCE GIRLS' (the 'A' grade key) green - fixed and covered by test_competency_ignores_ordinary_labels_containing_grade_letters.

ELASTIC WRAPPING (step 3): Global white-space:normal caused adjacent-cell tokens to merge (mean similarity fell to 99.77%, though glyphs stayed identical and no rows dropped), violating the exact-100% guarantee. Replaced with a targeted approach: model.Cell gains a `wrappable` flag; extract.build_table sets it only for single-line, non-rotated cells whose measured glyph width exceeds their own ruled column width (genuine overhang). html_out emits a `wrap` class for those cells and DOC_CSS adds `th.wrap,td.wrap{white-space:normal;overflow-wrap:break-word}` while the default stays nowrap. 35 cells across 6 documents now wrap inside their box. Verified 19/19 still at 100.00% with glyphs=identical (no rows dropped) and page counts unchanged.

CELL MERGING (step 4): Audited the compare images (SUBJECTWISE, SUBJECTS RANK, S1051, Schools Rank For Governments); header stacks (GPA/COMPETENCY LEVEL/RANK) and banner rows already merge correctly via classify.merge_header_stacks/peel_banner_rows. No cell in the references was found split in the output but merged in the reference, so no merging change was made (avoiding over-merge).

BEFORE/AFTER compare images (output/compare/*.jpg, regenerated): MWANZA CC 10 BEST SCHOOLS - DIVISION PERFORMANCE peach/orange/blue washes match; MWANZA CC SCHOOLS RANK SUBJECTWISE - competency Grade A/B green, Grade C yellow match and the transient green bleed into SCHOOL NAME/C-RANK columns (from the earlier over-eager fallback) is gone; MWANZA CC SUBJECTS RANK - Grade B/C/D + red F header + GPA green wash match; S1051-MKOLANI - cyan panel + yellow DETAILED SUBJECTS rows match cell-for-cell. Scratch diagnostic scripts were removed after use.

FILES CHANGED: NEW src/sars/competency.py; src/sars/extract.py (deterministic competency-colour fallback REMOVED from build_table - see REGRESSION FIX below; wrappable detection); src/sars/html_out.py (wrap class in _cell_html; th.wrap/td.wrap CSS); src/sars/model.py (Cell.wrappable); tests/test_sars.py (4 competency tests); regenerated output/{html,pdf,compare}/ artefacts and output/html/styles.css.

REGRESSION FIX (post-review correction): The deterministic-competency-colour FALLBACK originally added to extract.build_table was WRONG for the conversion/extraction path and caused a visible fidelity regression. In the reference PDF 'MWANZA CC 10 BEST SCHOOLS' page 1 the COMPETENCY LEVEL cells (Grade A/B/D...) have NO fill in the reference (plain white, black text), yet the fallback painted them solid green/yellow/orange. Requirement #1 is that the CONVERTED output match the reference cell-for-cell on colour; inventing a background where the reference has none is a regression. FIX: removed the fallback block (and the now-unused `from .competency import band_for_label` import) from extract.build_table. Conversion is now a faithful reproduction only - a cell's background is ONLY what _pick_background recovers from the actual PDF fill; where the reference leaves a competency cell white, the converted cell stays white. src/sars/competency.py is KEPT INTACT (BANDS, CUTOFFS=(1.5,2.5,3.5,4.5), band_for_gpa/band_for_label/resolve/background_for) and its 4 unit tests remain - the deterministic competency colour is reserved for the data-driven TEMPLATE/generation path (FEAT-004), where there is no PDF to extract from, NOT for faithful conversion. The elastic-wrapping work (model.Cell.wrappable + th.wrap/td.wrap CSS + build_table wrappable detection) is unchanged and retained.

RE-VERIFICATION after the fix: regenerated 'MWANZA CC 10 BEST SCHOOLS' and inspected the compare image - the COMPETENCY LEVEL cells are now WHITE/no-background matching the reference, while the DIVISION PERFORMANCE peach/orange/green tint washes are still present. Re-checked 'MWANZA CC SCHOOLS RANK SUBJECTWISE' and 'MWANZA CC SUBJECTS RANK': those reports DO colour competency cells in the reference and the colours still appear (Grade A/B green, C yellow, D orange, F red) because they come from real extracted fills, not the fallback. Full run: `sars all` = 19/19 pass, mean text similarity 100.00%, glyphs=identical; `pytest -q` = 29 passed; ruff + black clean (line-length 100) on all changed files. Regenerated ALL compare images via `python tools/compare.py`.
